article_title: Intelligent tutoring in dynamic domains: a graph-based system for comparative analysis of adaptive algorithms
citation: Csépányi-Fürjes, L., & Kovács, L. (2026). Intelligent tutoring in dynamic domains: a graph-based system for comparative analysis of adaptive algorithms with intuitionistic fuzzy logic and forgetting. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10639-6
title: Adapted IFL Interpretation Triangle for knowledge state visualization
description: The adapted Atanassov intuitionistic fuzzy logic triangle visualizes and classifies learner knowledge states per knowledge unit. The horizontal leg represents correct responses and the vertical leg incorrect responses; "The triangle vertices define three epistemic categories: point 'unknown' (origin, marked by '?'), point 'does not know' (top of the vertical leg, marked by 'X'), and point 'knows' (end of the horizontal leg, marked by '✓')." Threshold regions partition the triangle, and the system recommends the units whose estimated states are closest to the 'knows' vertex, prioritizing "units that the learner is most likely to master with minimal effort."
requirements: Measured mastery values per knowledge unit mapped onto the triangle, and predicted states propagated through the knowledge graph by the selected algorithm
constraints: The proximity-based recommendation deliberately deviates from classical KST outer-fringe recommendation, targeting medium to large knowledge units with partial content overlap rather than highly granular structures
target_learners: university students using the G4L system
target_learning_goals: understanding one's own knowledge state and deciding what to study next
examples: The teacher dashboard visualizes system-generated indicators via the adjusted IFL Interpretation Triangle
key_sources: Csépányi-Fürjes, L., & Kovács, L. (2026). Intelligent tutoring in dynamic domains: a graph-based system for comparative analysis of adaptive algorithms with intuitionistic fuzzy logic and forgetting. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10639-6

article_title: The Role of Individual Differences in Sourcing: a Systematic Review
citation: Anmarkrud, Ø., Bråten, I., Florit, E., & Mason, L. (2022). The Role of Individual Differences in Sourcing: a Systematic Review. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-021-09640-7
title: Integrated framework of multiple texts: four stance profiles differing in sourcing behavior
description: List and Alexander's integrated framework of multiple texts (IF-MT) describes preparation, execution, and production stages of multiple document use, with the preparation stage most important for individual differences. Readers adopt one of four stance profiles combining individual interest, attitudes, and multiple document proficiency: disengaged, affectively engaged, evaluative, and critical analytic. The review notes that "these four stance profiles are also assumed to differ in terms of their sourcing behavior", with evaluative and critical analytic readers sourcing frequently and only critical analytic readers using source information to reconcile conflicts. The review stresses these assumptions remain loosely grounded in evidence.
requirements: Stance adoption depends on combinations of individual interest, attitudes, and multiple document proficiency
constraints: The review states these assumptions "must be regarded as hypotheses that are fairly loosely grounded in empirical evidence"
examples: Readers with high interest, strong attitudes, and low proficiency are assumed to adopt an affectively engaged stance and source infrequently
key_sources: Anmarkrud, Ø., Bråten, I., Florit, E., & Mason, L. (2022). The Role of Individual Differences in Sourcing: a Systematic Review. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-021-09640-7

article_title: Enhancing Students' Learning: Instant Feedback Cards
citation: Lawrence C. Mohrweis & Kathe M. Shinham. (2015). Enhancing Students' Learning: Instant Feedback Cards. American Journal Of Business Education – First Quarter 2015 Volume 8, Number 1. https://www.cluteinstitute.com
title: IF-AT (Immediate Feedback Assessment Technique) scratch-off cards
description: IF-AT cards are commercially produced multiple-choice answer forms on which each answer option is covered by a waxy opaque coating similar to scratch-and-win lottery tickets. Students scratch their chosen answer: a star appears if correct, a blank space if not, and students "can then reconsider the options that remain and continue to scratch -off the boxes until the star is found". The authors obtained the cards from their campus faculty development center, sourced from Epstein Educational Enterprises, and used them as a low-cost review tool in introductory accounting.
requirements: Commercially produced IF-AT cards obtained at nominal cost (from a campus faculty development center or the Epstein Educational Company)
constraints: Students cannot change answers once the coating is scratched off
Cards cannot be computer graded; scores must be computed manually
target_learners: introductory accounting undergraduates (mostly traditional 18-20 year old students)
target_learning_goals: review of objective course content before midterm exams
examples: Two instructors used 25-question IF-AT forms (last five questions unused) in team review exercises of about 30 minutes of class time with 100 students
key_sources: Lawrence C. Mohrweis & Kathe M. Shinham. (2015). Enhancing Students' Learning: Instant Feedback Cards. American Journal Of Business Education – First Quarter 2015 Volume 8, Number 1. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1053380

article_title: An Investigation into the Recognition and Production of Pitch Patterns of "If"-Clauses by Turkish Pre-Service Teachers of English
citation: Topal, İ.H. (2018). An investigation into the recognition and production of pitch patterns of if-clauses by turkish pre-service teachers of english. Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies, 14(4), 285-300. http://www.jlls.org
title: Twelve-sentence If-clause pitch-pattern test corpus with written (recognition) and oral (production) forms
description: The main instrument is a corpus of 12 If-conditional sentences drawn from Longman dictionaries and course books, equally divided across Type 1, 2 and 3 conditionals, with the If-clause at the beginning in half and in the middle in the other half. The article states: "There were 12 If-conditional sentences of Type 1, 2, and 3 conditionals equally divided into 4 sentences in total for each conditional type." The written form assessed recognition via multiple choice and the oral form assessed production via read-aloud recordings. Reliability was supported: Cronbach's alpha was 0.73 (pre-test) and 0.74 (post-test) for the written test, and KR-20 was 0.79 and 0.77 for the oral test.
requirements: Sentences selected based on expert opinion from three experts and criteria such as sound quality and sentence length
target_learning_goals: Assessing recognition and production of If-clause pitch patterns
examples: Sentences were downloaded through the Audacity program at 44100 Hertz and illustrated with speech waves in Figures 1-12.
key_sources: Topal, İ.H. (2018). An investigation into the recognition and production of pitch patterns of if-clauses by turkish pre-service teachers of english. Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies, 14(4), 285-300. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1201884

article_title: Identifying core teamwork competencies for community-based health and social care professionals: an e-Delphi study.
citation: Aleo Giuseppe, Pagnucci Nicola, Walsh Niamh, Moriarty Frank, Giardulli Benedetto, Koutra Kleio, Przyłęcki Paweł, Fitzgerald Catherine, Illing Jan. (2026). Identifying core teamwork competencies for community-based health and social care professionals: an e-Delphi study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08478-9
title: Integrated Framework of Competencies (IFC) for community-based interprofessional teamwork
description: The IFC is the competency framework developed in the study's preliminary phase and refined through the e-Delphi rounds. It began as "a preliminary Integrated Framework of Competencies (IFC) was developed, consisting of 63 proposed core competencies divided into 5 areas" and was restructured after Round 2 into the final five-area structure covering teamwork, communication and conduct, shared vision, digital health, and care planning. It organises competencies by general thematic area, name, and brief description, structured to be articulated into learning outcomes using ECVET action verbs.
requirements: Competencies are articulated into learning outcomes using the ECVET list of action verbs to facilitate implementation and evaluation
constraints: The framework structure was modified after Round 2, with areas and sub-areas adjusted to improve coherence and eliminate redundancies
target_learners: Health and social care professionals working in Community-Based Interprofessional Teams
target_learning_goals: Transversal teamwork competencies for person-centred community-based care
examples: The preliminary IFC listed 63 competencies across five areas including 'Interprofessional Communication and Teamwork', 'Digital Health', and 'Soft Skills/Twenty-first Century Skills'
key_sources: Aleo Giuseppe, Pagnucci Nicola, Walsh Niamh, Moriarty Frank, Giardulli Benedetto, Koutra Kleio, Przyłęcki Paweł, Fitzgerald Catherine, Illing Jan. (2026). Identifying core teamwork competencies for community-based health and social care professionals: an e-Delphi study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08478-9
